511: 4 exhibitions in one day is a lot even for us, especially in just two teams. Michal Budský and Marek Tryner took a trip to far-off Pržno, where they enjoyed the local festival in front of a great audience.
512: {1}Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček with his complete kids' line-up headed Prague – Sokolov – Karlovy Vary. First up was Pražské služby, where together with the guys from Flow parkour they rode an exhibition in front of loads of spectators, who weren't put off even by the 29-degree scorcher.
513: Next was the Czech Masters Road Cycling Championship organised by Cyklokili, with the awards ceremony on Sokolov square. A beautifully organised event, limited only by road closures on the course due to reconstruction work. And of course, who's a better spectator than a cyclist 🙂.
514: Last up was Otovice near Karlovy Vary. A really polished village, where the locals put on a great event full of performances and rock music. We could barely drag the obstacles out of the trailer by then, but we got fired up and the spectators were incredible. We couldn't deprive them of crashes either – this time, unusually, it was Martin Šimůnek who took care of that. In the heat of battle he even flew onto his backside from over a metre and sat on the wireless microphone :) Even a world champion falls during a show once every 20 years. But the exhibition was successfully completed.
515: Sports clubs' ball exhibition – Kralupy nad Vltavou
516: The sports clubs' ball was a big surprise. 600+ spectators, the great setting of the cultural centre hall and loads of side programme for sportsmen and sportswomen. Vlasta, Lukáš Valný and Tobík Dolák even had plenty of space backstage for a warm-up, which had its own spectators. The waxed floor was a bit of a struggle, and there were a few crowd-pleasing crashes (luckily on the flat and harmless). After the classic intro on the obstacles we moved on to the male and female volunteers. The highlight was a riders vs walkers high-jump battle. It was no surprise that on the slippery floor the jumper without a bike won, but nobody expected it to be a rugby player. Thanks for the warm welcome and the cheering – hopefully we'll meet on a bigger scale at a summer event.
518: An exhibition marathon by the BIKESKILLS guys
519: Here are a few reports on the travels of our BIKESKILLS instructors, who don't just teach but keep spreading joy at Trial exhibitions all over the Czech Republic. When it's allowed, that is :)
521: Rain all day, but beautiful weather exactly for the moment of the exhibition. As they say, more luck than judgement for Lukáš Valný and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, who set off for a quick exhibition literally through the forest from where they live. The kids were going wild in the rain at the Olympics, so the performance by our team and club – in nice weather, too – was a lovely change. For us it was a warm-up before the upcoming marathon of exhibitions in September.
522: {1}6 Sep 2020 – Brno Sports Day – KS Omega Brno{2}
523: Marek Tryner kicked off a series of exhibitions in Brno, where he finished his studies a few years ago. Little Jířa Sehnal appeared alongside him as a guest, and together they entertained the boys and girls at the event.
524: {1}11 Sep 2020 – Road trade fair exhibition – Pardubice{2}
525: Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček met up in Pardubice at a trade fair focused on road transport. In beautiful sunny weather the grounds of the local services company attracted a real crowd of visitors who weren't afraid of the coronavirus and appreciated the guys' performance, which somewhat blocked the space in front of the main stage. There was also an interview for local TV – the usual :)
526: {1}12 Sep 2020 – 3 exhibitions in one day – Rouské / Nový Bor / Prague-Zeleneč{2}
527: Today, for the first time this year, we got out all our mobile parks and vehicles. Marek Tryner and Lukáš Valný went to the village of Rouské (South Moravia), where they showed a bit of Trial action at the local fair, having first managed to enjoy some trails on mountain bikes. Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Michal Budský set off with the trailer to Nový Bor, where Martin Šimůnek was already waiting at the employee days of Crystalex. On the company premises employees and their families had loads of attractions and, besides concerts, two shows by our team. Martin Šimůnek then went to a smaller event (unfortunately we don't know where yet :)), and Vlasta and Michal drove at the maximum permitted speed to Prague-Zeleneč, where a children's day was being held on the local meadows. They didn't have much energy left, but Michal fired up a bottle-hitting contest when jumping off the trailer, and Vlasta, despite a brace on his leg, tried to push his sideways jump record. He ended at 127 cm over the tape (3 cm below the official Czech record), which isn't bad after 6 knee operations.
528: {1}13 Sep 2020 – Exhibition at the fair – Škvorec{2}
529: As is often the case, we don't ride many exhibitions near our homes. We're usually booked from further away. The same actually happened now – Martin Šimůnek was originally supposed to ride the exhibition, but by coincidence it ended up on our club and team shoulders :) The local fair by the stage became a Trial park for a few hours for Vlasta, Marek, Lukáš and Matouš Balík. But the club's little ones also came along to watch or test the test course we'd put together.
530: {1}18 and 19 Sep 2020 – Říčany town festival and an individual course in Trutnov{2}
531: Normally we don't mention individual training much in our reports, but we'll make an exception as part of this marathon. Marek Tryner was coaching in Prague, while Vlasta was on the Trutnov trails as part of the BIKESKILLS project. Vlasta then went wild with Lukáš Valný and young Mrlik from the club at the town festival in Říčany, where poor attendance was very noticeable – people were evidently afraid. Normally this festival is a very popular event in the Říčany area. The exhibition spot was deliberately chosen on the local cycle path away from the main event, so there were practically only spectators while the peloton on historic bikes passed, but on the other hand we had the chance to ride more.
533: We held a camp for women, girls and female bikers, where Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček coached alongside Katarína Tóthová a group of enthusiastic female bikers who wanted to improve and enjoy off-road riding more. There was some egging on at the steps and descents too. The great weather only underlined the pleasant atmosphere of the camp.{1}{2}
534: Exhibition in Sadská, or 'Lines on Top'
535: The exhibitions in Sadská are a beautiful example of a community event organised by the cultural centre and the local volunteer fire brigade
536: There was nothing to fault about the event – beautiful weather, active spectators and even the deputy mayor, pulled out by mistake as a volunteer.
537: Hopefully our riding by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Lukáš Valný and Ondra Nenadál entertained kids and adults – thanks for the invitation.
539: You don't turn down an invitation from a partner – and certainly not when it's to the second-biggest cycling race in the world, the Giro d'Italia, whose first stages were ridden in Budapest. Thanks to {1}Levelsportkoncept{2} – specifically POC, the brand I've ridden for for most of my sporting career – my colleague Marek Tryner and I had the chance to experience the atmosphere of such a big event and watch road cycling from the front line.
540: The exhibition itself took place in a beautiful central park near the start. We had both our team trailer and partners' branded obstacles on site. The sound system was occupied by the broadcast on the big screen, but in the end we found a way to lure spectators to our exhibitions and do a bit of hosting in English. Riding the obstacles was also great training, which sometimes got out of hand and we rode for a few hours straight.
541: Everything hurts, but hopefully both POC and the spectators were happy – for them it was a very unusual thing compared with the time trials of the guys on road bikes.
542: Camp dates for women and men are out
543: The Bikeskills camps are out and we hope to see you on the bike as often as possible. The number of exhibitions our riders do slows us down a bit, but hopefully we've managed to get most events into our yellow calendar. We may add one more spring date – please give us time. Even so, we're offering a third more camps than last year, which will hopefully fully satisfy you and take your technique to the next level.
544: Of course you can also use our individual courses and put together a small group of friends. We'll take you through challenging trails and to secret spots.
545: If you'd like to sign up for a camp and don't see it in the camp list yet, write to {1}info@bikeskills.cz{2}. We announce camps gradually.
546: Day camp and exhibitions in Loučná and Žulová
547: We have a tough week behind us. Unfortunately it started badly with Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček's injury in a bike park (ribs, sternum and spine). Luckily Vlasta walked away on his own feet, but still, not great. Thank goodness it didn't jeopardise the bike day camp during the week, and 25 boys and girls could throw themselves into improving on bikes under the supervision of Bikeskills instructors and capable carers from our club. Kids come back to us year after year and you can see their progress – including boys who win Enduro races for the youngest.
548: At the weekend Martin Šimůnek and Lukáš Valný headed to exhibitions in Loučná (workshop with a show) and Žulová in the Jeseníky mountains (concerts at the town festival). The guys worked their socks off in the prevailing heat.
549: Exhibition by the Bikeskills guys at the Around the Republic race
550: The very idea of riding around the whole Czech Republic by bike is exhausting for me, and respect to everyone who voluntarily signs up for this event as a rider. Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Mára Tryner and Matouš Balík from our club were riders too – but luckily only with a Trial show, which they put on at the start in the morning.
551: In half an hour they showed both classic Trial and overcoming obstacles on regular mountain bikes. Hopefully it whetted the participants' appetite a bit and they decided that rather than risk the obstacles, they'll do those 1,400 kilometres.
552: Thanks for the invitation – hopefully everyone gets through those few days safely. From the exhibition the guys went straight to the Trutnov trails, where they flew down the black routes – Ptačí perspektiva deserves special praise. It has some really well-made rocky sections, though you could figure out a few harder lines there :)
554: Vlasta reports on building the trail in Říčany:
555: {1}As I wrote earlier, I was approached to build the Olivova trail in my home town of Říčany. There was a very limited budget, and therefore a challenge to do something for the community. I'm an organiser and I have no problem building a natural trail, but a flow trail with jumps is outside my field. After selecting possible builders we went for Kuba Vencl, who used to ride there with local Honza Tóth, and who even got a machine operator's licence for the project. Everything important was sorted, and construction started a few weeks ago. The weather sometimes threw a spanner in the works, but the guys worked fast and the few problems along the way were solved quickly. Today is probably the last day of construction, finishing the surface. I'm attaching a few photos that I think will please every biker's eye. Our club should take over management of the area, and the Bikeskills project will have another place to train on the Tehov – Říčany route.{2}
556: {1}For next year I'm preparing two events, one of which will be the season opener and the official opening of the trail, which won't happen this year anymore. It will include a workshop, a dirt jump exhibition and a Trial exhibition.{2}
557: Exhibition at the camping festival in Chvalovice with a pump track workshop
558: A really tricky event. A bit of confusion in the programme – at the organiser's request we tried to set off half a day earlier – wouldn't have mattered much. If we can, we try to accommodate everyone. But a burst tyre on the car delayed us by almost 4 hours. Luckily we had time in reserve, so in the end the exhibition simply took place at the agreed time in the nice leisure park in Chvalovice, led by Vlasta and Lukáš with the little ones. Katarína Tóthová, thanks to our mobile sound system, took care of a workshop on the nearby pump track.
559: Bike blessing, a bikers' wedding and Safety Days
560: On the first weekend of May we had a double exhibition at the Bike Blessing in Dolní Branná, where we rode two shows on a newly built playground near the local church. Together with Martin Šimůnek we prepared a workshop with an obstacle course for the local kids, and despite the initial rain quite a lot of locals and visitors came.
561: Straight from Dolní Branná we headed for Most, where two bikers were getting married at the Rudolice farmstead. Dad's a cyclist and the kids ride trails and bike parks. A few guests were slightly tipsy, but most were saving themselves for our surprise, arranged by the bride's mother. All the best in life to the newlyweds and to the wedding guests who lay down under our wheels 🙂
562: The following weekend safety was on the agenda in front of a shopping centre in Teplice. This big event, attended by practically all organisations focused on safety and the rescue services, has an almost 20-year tradition, and you could tell from the turnout. Events at shopping centres are usually a bit boring, but a decent number of people came here and the organisation was high quality too. So Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček rode slightly sharper and longer shows. The first had light rain at the end, but the second was spot on.
